Consult Summary:
- A physically active patient reports new right knee pain with mechanical symptoms (knee clicking) beginning about 2 weeks ago after increasing long-distance training for a marathon. Pain emerges around 2–3 miles into runs, with an earlier episode of mild swelling; right knee is affected, left knee unaffected. She also notes a transient tingling sensation in the right toes after runs.
- Plan includes conservative management (ice therapy, reduced running), NSAID optimization with a stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed, and referral to physiotherapy for a knee assessment with consideration of imaging if symptoms persist or worsen. Urgent evaluation instructions provided if red flags (swelling with heat/redness, fever, knee completely locked) occur.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Description: Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms (clicking) starting ~2 weeks ago, during increased marathon training; pain begins after about 20 minutes of running (mile 2–3); prior mild swelling; right knee more involved than left; ROM reported as full (can straighten and flex fully); no current swelling or locking; feels instability only mildly when asked.
- Associated symptoms: Clicking on knee during flexion/extension; intermittent swelling earlier; no significant instability reported; no difficulty with stairs or walking; no color or temperature changes.
- Exam findings (patient-reported): ROM intact; no current swelling; no locking detected on interview; prior suggestion of knee effusion by patient.
- Social history/Medications: Marathon training; plays sports (ice hockey in past); takes ibuprofen 400 mg as needed (dose/frequency not documented); uses Aleve occasionally; Vitamin D; Melatonin; Xanax PRN; cannabis use.
- Differential/Consult review: Overuse knee injury due to increased distance running; possible cartilage involvement considered; ACL-related injury discussed by patient but not diagnosed via video; imaging not yet performed; physiotherapy first recommended; imaging considered if persistent/worsening symptoms.

Issue 2:
- Description: Transient tingling in the right toes after running (one episode); no persistent numbness or color/temperature changes; no ongoing neuropathic symptoms reported.
- Associated symptoms: Tingling occurred once post-run; otherwise normal sensation returned.
- Exam findings: Not specifically documented beyond patient report.
- Plan: Not specifically enumerated beyond overall knee management; no dedicated treatment plan for neuropathic symptom provided.

Issue 3:
- Description: Analgesia/medication plan in context of knee pain.
- Plan/management: Continue ice therapy; ease up on running if pain is limiting; ibuprofen allowed; provider offered a slightly stronger anti-inflammatory to be prescribed (to be taken regularly, not with ibuprofen, and with food). A referral to physiotherapy is planned, with possible imaging if indicated after assessment.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — 400 mg, as needed; dose/route/frequency not fully documented.
- Naproxen (Aleve) — dose/route/frequency not documented; used occasionally.
- Vitamin D — dose not documented.
- Melatonin — dose not documented.
- Xanax — dose not documented (PRN use).
- Acetaminophen not clearly confirmed as being used (unclear from transcript).

Allergies:
- None documented.

Past Medical History:
- Lasik surgery.
- Significant prior UTI with suspicion for kidney stones; ER visit; reference to morphine exposure during that event.
- Described as generally healthy aside from common illnesses.

Social History:
- Marathon training for upcoming race; regular gym activity.
- Past ice hockey injury with a large bruise.
- Cannabis use (smokes joints).
- Other social history not detailed (e.g., tobacco, alcohol).

Preventative History:
- Not documented in the transcript (no cervical, breast, prostate screening, vaccinations, or other preventive measures noted).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Knee exam: No current swelling; full ROM (able to straighten and flex); no locking reported on interview; right knee predominantly involved with clicking during movement; no focal exam findings explicitly described; tenderness to palpation not confirmed; patient reports prior effusion.
- Neurological/vascular: Transient tingling in right toes after running; no persistent numbness; no color/temperature changes in legs reported.

Plan:
- Continue ice therapy as tolerated.
- Ease up on running; discontinue or reduce running if pain worsens.
- Ibuprofen may be continued; consider prescription of a stronger NSAID to be taken regularly, with instruction to avoid concurrent use with ibuprofen and to take with food.
- Refer to physiotherapist for comprehensive knee assessment and examination.
- Imaging (e.g., knee imaging/cartilage evaluation) to be considered after physiotherapist assessment if indicated.
- If persistent swelling, warmth, redness, fever, or knee completely locks, contact urgent care/doctor.
- If awaiting physiotherapy, clinic visit is available as an alternative.
- Pharmacy to receive prescription for stronger anti-inflammatory.
